founded.what: The year Nicolas François Billecart and Elisabeth Salmon married and founded the house at Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, by the house's own history.

place: Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, Vallée de la Marne, Champagne

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: it grows grapes, buys more from growers across Champagne and makes the wine itself in its cellars at Mareuil-sur-Aÿ.

story: Billecart-Salmon began in 1818, when Nicolas François Billecart married Elisabeth Salmon at Mareuil-sur-Aÿ and the couple founded a Champagne house there; her brother joined them in the business, and accounts differ over which of the two men made the wine and which sold it. Their descendants ran it through the generations. In 1958 the son of the fourth generation changed the cellar: the juice was settled cold and fermented long and at low temperature, which gave the house the restraint it is known for. With the 1964 vintage the house made the first Cuvée Nicolas François, named in homage to the founder, by its own history; one account traces the blend to the 1955 vintage. The same year Pinot Noir was planted in the walled vineyard beside the house, the Clos Saint-Hilaire, by the house's account. Cuvée Elisabeth Salmon, a vintage rosé named for the founder's wife, was first made with the 1988 vintage and released in 2001. In 1993, by the house's account, it bought its stock back from the supermarkets. The Clos gave its first vintage in 1995. In the middle of the 2000s the Frey family's investment company took a minority share of 45 per cent, the year given as 2004 or 2005 by different accounts, and the family kept the majority.

style.line: Restraint and finesse with a very fine mousse: since 1958 the juice has been settled cold and fermented long and cool, mainly in stainless steel, with oak kept for part of the prestige wines.
style.grapes: All three grapes. For Nicolas François the Pinot Noir comes from the Montagne de Reims and the Grande Vallée de la Marne and the Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs, by the house.
style.reserve: Over half of the Brut Réserve is reserve wine, by the house: over 55 per cent on its current page and over 50 on another.
style.vessels: Mainly stainless steel at low temperature, by the house, with oak casks for part of Nicolas François and all of Le Clos Saint-Hilaire.
style.malolactic: Partial for Nicolas François 2008, by the house's page for that vintage.
style.lees: About 50 months for the Brut Réserve on the house's current pages, 30 on an older sheet; more than ten years for Nicolas François 2008.
style.dosage: Very low on the prestige wines: 2.9 grams a litre for Nicolas François 2008 and about 2 for Le Clos Saint-Hilaire 2009, by the house.

nv.name: Brut Réserve
nv.note: The non vintage Brut a guest meets first, over half of it reserve wine by the house; the Brut Rosé is the house's other calling card, and many guests know the house by it.

cuvee.name: Cuvée Nicolas François

first.what: The first vintage under the founder's name, by the house; one account traces the blend to the 1955 vintage, named only with the 1964.

cuvee.rhythm: Made only in the years the house declares: its own pages show the 2002, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2012 vintages. A 1959 is known under the name too, though the house dates the cuvée from 1964.
cuvee.blend: Pinot Noir, about three fifths, with Chardonnay for the rest, as the house states for the 2008 vintage; no Meunier.
cuvee.sites: Grand and Premier Cru villages, about five sixths Grand Cru in the 2008: the Pinot Noir from Aÿ, Verzenay and Mareuil-sur-Aÿ among others, the Chardonnay from Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Chouilly and Cramant. The 2012 sheet adds Avize.
cuvee.making: The juice is settled cold and fermented at low temperature, most of it in stainless steel and about a sixth in oak casks for the 2008, by the house, with malolactic conversion partial. The bottles then rest more than ten years on their lees before disgorging, and the dosage is very low: 2.9 grams a litre for the 2008.
cuvee.lees: More than ten years for the 2008 on the house's page; its technical sheet for the vintage gives about 150 months.
cuvee.young: Lemon curd and lime over brioche and praline, with a little apricot and mandarin zest, toast and honey, a salty edge and a firm, precise line.
cuvee.aged: With bottle age it turns to apricot jam, honey and truffle on buttered toast, as merchants' notes on the 2002 describe; Decanter found dried lime, caramel, hay and mocha in the 1986.
cuvee.serve: 9 to 11 degrees Celsius, the Codex's range for a fuller, partly oak fermented Champagne; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass. The house's pages read give no figure.

also.name: Le Clos Saint-Hilaire

first.what: The first vintage of the cuvée, by the house's own page and the library.

also.note: A single walled vineyard of one hectare beside the house at Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, planted to Pinot Noir from 1964 and made as a vintage Blanc de Noirs from 1995. It is fermented wholly in oak casks and finished with very little dosage, about 2 grams a litre for the 2009, by the house. The class sheet prints it first, as Clos St. Hilaire: learn it as the house's second prestige wine, made beside Nicolas François.
also.line: Le Clos Saint-Hilaire is Billecart-Salmon's walled vineyard of Pinot Noir beside the house, a Blanc de Noirs first made in 1995.

table.house45: Billecart-Salmon is a family house of Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, in the Vallée de la Marne, founded in 1818 when Nicolas François Billecart married Elisabeth Salmon. It carries both their names, and their descendants ran it through the generations. From 1958 the house settled its juice cold and fermented it long and cool. That gives the restraint and the very fine bubbles it is known for. Its Brut Rosé is the wine many guests already know. Cuvée Nicolas François is the prestige cuvée, named for the founder. Beside the house lies Le Clos Saint-Hilaire, a walled vineyard of Pinot Noir with a wine of its own.
table.house10: Billecart-Salmon is the family house of Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, founded in 1818 and known for its restraint and its rosé.
table.cuvee45: Cuvée Nicolas François is the vintage prestige cuvée of Billecart-Salmon, named for the man who founded the house in 1818. It is about three fifths Pinot Noir and two fifths Chardonnay, mostly from Grand Cru villages such as Aÿ, Verzenay and Cramant. A small part is fermented in oak, and the wine then rests more than ten years in the cellar before release. It is finished almost dry. Expect lemon curd, brioche and praline, with a salty edge and a firm line. I pour it a little warmer than most Champagne, in a tulip glass.
table.sale: If you like Champagne with depth and a dry, precise finish, Cuvée Nicolas François rests more than ten years in the cellar before it reaches the table. May I bring a bottle for you?
table.cuvee10: Cuvée Nicolas François is Billecart-Salmon's vintage prestige cuvée, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay named for the founder.
table.cuvee20: Cuvée Nicolas François is the prestige cuvée of Billecart-Salmon, a vintage blend of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay first sold under that name with the 1964. It rests more than ten years in the cellar and is finished almost dry.

guests.q: Which is Billecart's true prestige cuvée, Nicolas François or the Clos?
guests.a: Both are prestige wines. Cuvée Nicolas François is the vintage blend a guest meets most, and Le Clos Saint-Hilaire is a single walled vineyard of Pinot Noir beside the house, made from 1995 and far rarer.

guests.q: Is Mareuil-sur-Aÿ a Grand Cru village?
guests.a: No, it is Premier Cru. The house's prestige blends draw mostly on Grand Cru villages, Aÿ and Verzenay among them, with Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs.

guests.q: Does the house make a rosé prestige cuvée?
guests.a: Yes, Cuvée Elisabeth Salmon, a vintage rosé named for the co-founder, first made with the 1988 vintage and released in 2001. It is a different wine from Nicolas François.

traps: Clos Saint-Hilaire is a blanc de noirs from Pinot Noir, not Chardonnay.
Mareuil-sur-Aÿ is premier cru, not grand cru: the house's own village is not a Grand Cru.
The class sheet is cut off after Franco: the cuvée is Nicolas François, named for the founder, and the sheet's first name, Clos St. Hilaire, is the walled vineyard wine.
Cuvée Nicolas François is named for the founder and Cuvée Elisabeth Salmon, the vintage rosé, for his wife: two prestige wines of the one house.

sheet.label: Le Clos Saint-Hilaire; Cuvée Nicolas François
sheet.note: The sheet writes Saint as St., drops the Le and is cut off at the page edge after Franco: the name is Nicolas François. Labels and the house's own pages have read both Cuvée Nicolas François Billecart and Cuvée Nicolas François.

cards.front: Billecart-Salmon: name its vintage prestige cuvée and its walled vineyard wine.
cards.back: Cuvée Nicolas François, and Le Clos Saint-Hilaire. The class sheet prints Clos St. Hilaire/Cuvée Nicolas Franco.

cards.front: Cuvée Nicolas François: which house makes it, and in which village?
Billecart-Salmon's walled vineyard wine, Le Clos Saint-Hilaire: which grape, and what first vintage?
cards.back: Pinot Noir alone, a Blanc de Noirs, first made in the 1995 vintage from the walled vineyard beside the house.

questions.q: On the class sheet, which house is paired with Clos St. Hilaire and Cuvée Nicolas François?
questions.exp: Billecart-Salmon names Nicolas François for its founder and makes Le Clos Saint-Hilaire beside the house. Philipponnat's single vineyard is the Clos des Goisses, Krug's the Clos du Mesnil, and Laurent-Perrier's prestige cuvée is Grand Siècle.

questions.q: From 1958, what did Billecart-Salmon change in its cellar that shapes its style?
opts: Cold settling and long, cool fermentation
Fermenting every wine in new oak
Ageing its reserve wines in magnum
questions.exp: From 1958 the house settled its juice cold and fermented it long and at low temperature, the root of its restraint. Reserve wines kept in magnum are Bollinger's mark, and the house uses oak only in part.

questions.q: By the house's own figures, how is Cuvée Nicolas François 2008 blended?
opts: About three fifths Pinot Noir, two fifths Chardonnay
Pinot Noir alone, from one walled vineyard
Equal thirds of the three grapes
questions.exp: The 2008 is about three fifths Pinot Noir and two fifths Chardonnay, mostly Grand Cru. Pinot Noir from one walled vineyard is the house's Clos Saint-Hilaire, and Chardonnay alone from Le Mesnil-sur-Oger is Salon.

sources.title: Decanter: Wine Legend, Cuvée Nicolas François 1959

report: kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label; the house buys grapes beyond its own vines by its own account of its villages, so a refuter should read a back label.

The founders are named only as the label names them (Nicolas François, Elisabeth Salmon); their dates were not found in two sources, nor were her brother's, so he is described, and since accounts differ over which man made the wine the record does not say.
The fourth generation's dates (1886 to 1963) are on the house's timeline alone, and his son who changed the cellar in 1958 may be living, so both are described and not named.
The Frey share is dated as the middle of the 2000s because sources give 2004 and 2005; the 45 per cent is the share bought, told as history.

Cuvée Elisabeth Salmon is kept out of cuvee.forms because it is a different name and wine, though the plan's note calls it the rosé form; its first vintage is 1988, released in 2001, by Decanter and Falstaff.

The label's name: the house's pages head the 1959 as Cuvée Nicolas François Billecart and the 2008 as Cuvée Nicolas François, and merchants print both for the 2002 and the 2008, so the record does not date the change.
Left out: the 1959 and 1961 placings at a tasting of 1999, a ranking; the Brut Réserve's blend and dosage (one search summary called it Extra Brut, which was not trusted); the Brut Rosé's making.
The service temperature is the Codex's range, since no house figure was found.

No tension with the library: the record keeps 1818, the Clos's 1995 first vintage, its Pinot Noir and Mareuil's Premier Cru standing, and adds the Clos's single hectare and first planting of 1964 from the house's page.
The house's store titles its non vintage Brut as Le Réserve in places; the record follows the list and the house's collection page, Brut Réserve.

changed: story: the brother's part (he made the wine, by the house) was cut; accounts read by the refuter give the division of labour both ways, so the story says they differ.
story and cuvee.first: the 1955 origin is now one account (Quill & Pad), not Decanter's; the house's own history and its 2008 sheet date the cuvée from 1964 as an homage to the founder.

cuvee.rhythm: the 1959 and 1961 told as made before the wine had its name was cut; a 1959 is known under the name (Decanter's Wine Legend), so the record says only that the house dates the cuvée from 1964.
story and a guest's answer: Cuvée Elisabeth Salmon is first made with the 1988 vintage and released in 2001 (Decanter, Falstaff), where the record said only created in 1988.
story: the 1993 turn to independent merchants and restaurants was cut; the house's history gives the buying back of stock from supermarkets and no more.
questions[0].exp: Philipponnat's Clos des Goisses is called a single vineyard, not a walled one, since its walls were not sourced.
Sources: Decanter's producer profile, which backed only the 1955 claim now given to Quill & Pad, was replaced by Decanter's Elisabeth Salmon 2008 masterclass.
open: NM was not read on a label; a merchant says the house buys grapes and is a négociant manipulant.
The Frey share of 45 per cent is confirmed by Agra (undated); its year, 2004 or 2005, stays unsettled.
How the 1959 was labelled, and whether a 1955 was made as the same wine, is not settled.
The 60 per cent of Pinot Noir in the 2008 rests on the house's 40 per cent of Chardonnay as the remainder.
